definitions.explanation: A hairless, thick-bodied caterpillar, typically of a moth or butterfly. The word specifically refers to the plump, smooth type (not hairy caterpillars, which are called 毛虫). Originally named for caterpillars found on sweet potato plants.

examples.japanese: {葉|は}っぱに{芋虫|いもむし}がいた。
examples.english: There was a caterpillar on a leaf.

examples.japanese: {芋虫|いもむし}はやがて{蝶|ちょう}になる。
examples.english: A caterpillar eventually becomes a butterfly.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}のキャベツを{見|み}たら、{芋虫|いもむし}がたくさんついていた。
examples.english: When I looked at the cabbages in the garden, there were a lot of caterpillars on them.

notes:
USAGE:
{芋虫|いもむし} refers specifically to smooth, hairless caterpillars. Hairy caterpillars are called {毛虫|けむし}. The name comes from {芋|いも} (sweet potato/taro) + {虫|むし} (insect), as these caterpillars were commonly found on potato plants.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {芋虫|いもむし}が{這|は}う: a caterpillar crawls
- {芋虫|いもむし}が{蛹|さなぎ}になる: a caterpillar becomes a chrysalis
- {青|あお}い{芋虫|いもむし}: a green caterpillar
